 Order

This appeal by the insurance company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 22.12.2016 passed by MACT, Ratlam in claim case no.76/13 seeking exoneration from the liability to pay compensation/reduction of amount of compensation.

1 2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that on 02.02.2013 at 01.00 PM deceased Rahul aged 10 years was playing outside his house, village Ponbatta when offending vehicle TATA magic bearing Engine No.C-6B-14961, chasis no.C-6- B-40287, model 2012 which was being driven by respondent no.3 rashly and negligently hit the deceased due to which he received injuries and died.
3. Claimants who are the parents of the deceased filed a claim petition against the appellant and respondents no.3 & 4 before the Tribunal.
The appellant and respondents no.3 & 4 filed their written statement and denied the averments.

4. The Tribunal framed issues on the basis of the pleadings and after taking evidence allowed the claim petition and awarded a compensation of Rs.3,45,000/- with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization against the appellant (insurance company) and respondents no.3 & 4 (driver and owner) jointly and severally.
Being aggrieved by the said award, the appellant/insurance company has filed this appeal seeking exoneration from liability/reduction of amount of compensation.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that Tribunal has committed error of law, facts and jurisdiction in passing the impugned award.
He submits that Tribunal has committed mistake in exonerating the appellant when it came to the conclusion that the vehicle was not plying under a permit and fitness certificate.
The Tribunal has committed error in holding that the driver was bringing the vehicle to home at the time of accident.

The Tribunal has committed mistake in deducting 1/3 amount towards personal expenses whereas it ought to have been 1/2.
6.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents supported the impugned award on the ground of liability fixed by the tribunal and filed a cross objection under Order 41 Rule 22 CPC CPC seeking enhancement of compensation.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant opposes the cross objection filed by the claimants.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the record it is found that the Tribunal in para-22 of the impugned award has held that owner of the offending vehicle was unable to produce the fitness certificate and permit of the offending vehicle.
So it is clearly established that owner of the offending vehicle was unable to produce the permit and fitness certificate of the offending vehicle.

10. In the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Vinod and others - 2020 (1) MPLJ 142 the co-ordinate Bench of this Court has held that permit and fitness certificate are essential requirements of the offending vehicle but due to non-availability of the permit and fitness certificate the offending vehicle was being used contrary to the provisions of law and in absence of permit and fitness certificate the insurance company would not be liable to indemnify the insured.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Vinod and others - 2020 (1) MPLJ 142
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
So in the considered opinion of this Court since the offending vehicle was not having the fitness certificate and permit at the time of accident, therefore, the terms and conditions of the insurance policy were Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd vs Nahar on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178318452/
2 violated.

entities.text: Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd vs Nahar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the insurance company is not jointly and severally liable to make payment of compensation in the case.

However, in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Amrit Paul Singh vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. - 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC) 8 the insurance company shall be liable to make payment of compensation with liberty to recover the same from the owner.

entities.text: Amrit Paul Singh vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd. - 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC) 8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So the finding of the Tribunal in this regard is modified to the aforesaid extent.
11. The appellant/insurance company has filed this appeal also for reduction of the amount of compensation.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants have filed a cross objection seeking enhancement of compensation.
12. After perusal of the record of the Tribunal it is found that at the time of accident the deceased was ten years of old.
In the case of Kishan Gopal and another vs. Lala and others - 2014 (2) MPLJ 569 the Apex Court has awarded a compensation of Rs.5 lakhs to the claimants for the death of a boy aged ten years.

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and another vs. Lala and others - 2014 (2) MPLJ 569
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case also the deceased was a boy aged ten years old, so in the light of the aforesaid verdict of the apex Court Kishan Gopal (supra) the claimants are entitled to get a compensation of Rs.5 lakhs in all heads as total amount of compensation.
13. Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.5,00,000/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.3,45,000/-.
Accordingly, the claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,55,000/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
14. In the result, the appeal as well as cross objection are allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

15. The respondents/claimants have valued the cross objection only to the extent of Rs.1,50,000/-
and paid the Court fee accordingly, however, for the remaining amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the claimants within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
16. In the result, the appeal as well cross objection are allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
